requirements.requirement: node1 has at least 512 MB of compressed in-memory (zram) swap configured
requirements.summary: Playbook configured zram-size = max(ram/2, 512) with zstd compression; swapon --show confirms /dev/zram0 at 980M, well above the 512MB minimum, both immediately after configuration (cmd-c09082325cf547f1) and after a full reboot (cmd-81353ad6c78c4127).

requirements.requirement: swap is compressed in-memory (zram, not disk-backed)
requirements.summary: /sys/block/zram0/comp_algorithm shows zstd selected as the active algorithm, confirmed both right after setup and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: zram swap is preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: swapon --show shows /dev/zram0 at priority 100 versus the pre-existing /dev/vda3 disk swap at priority -2 (higher priority is used first), verified both before and after node1's reboot.

requirements.requirement: zram swap is active at boot (persists across restart without manual intervention)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id d9f8550d was captured pre-reboot; systemctl reboot was issued; connection dropped and recovered; new boot_id 5d081df6 confirmed by the fixed after_executor snapshot; zram0 swap was automatically active at 980M/zstd/priority 100 post-boot with no manual re-activation, and generator-managed dev-zram0.swap is wired into swap.target.

An Ansible playbook (/root/ansible-zram/zram-swap.yml) was written and run from node2 (the designated Ansible control node) against node1 via inventory, performing package install, config file management, and service activation through Ansible modules; a second idempotent run (changed=0) after node2's own reboot confirms the control path and playbook logic both work correctly.

requirements.requirement: Independent node-restart evidence protocol: node1 pre-restart baseline, restart, new boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: node1 baseline boot_id/uptime/swap captured healthy, systemctl reboot issued, connection drop and recovery polled through timeouts/resets, new boot_id 5d081df6 confirmed distinct from baseline d9f8550d (matches fixed after_executor snapshot), and swap/zram/service state fully recovered and healthy post-boot.

requirements.requirement: Independent node-restart evidence protocol: node2 pre-restart baseline, restart, new boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: node2 baseline boot_id 416c5cf5 captured, reboot issued, connection drop/recovery polled, new boot_id 57fcc8a9 confirmed (matches fixed after_executor snapshot), and Ansible control-plane functionality independently verified recovered via SSH to node1 and a successful idempotent playbook re-run.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 has ~980MB of zstd-compressed zram swap configured via an Ansible playbook run from the node2 control node, at priority 100 (preferred over the pre-existing disk swap at -2), and confirmed active automatically after a full reboot with a changed boot identity. The independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for both node1 and node2, each showing a clean baseline, restart acknowledgement, new boot identity matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and full recovery (including Ansible control-plane functionality from node2 to node1). No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found beyond prerequisites directly tied to the task or the restart protocol.
limitations: Evidence for node2's post-reboot recovered state relies on functional verification (SSH + idempotent playbook run) rather than a full independent lifecycle re-snapshot of node2's disk/service state, though this is sufficient given node2 has no persistent service to verify beyond SSH/Ansible availability.

The zram-generator package verification for post-reboot state relies on swapon/systemctl/sysfs output rather than an explicit 'rpm -q zram-generator' re-check after reboot, though functional swap activity is direct proof of correct package state.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological command trace, state-changing actions were: adding the cluster SSH pubkey to node1's authorized_keys (cmd-eef9be160f4d402e) and writing the cluster private key on node2 (cmd-80e2fa5124334712), both necessary prerequisites for the Ansible control path given node2 is the designated controller; zram-generator package install and config write (part of cmd-c09082325cf547f1's playbook run), directly required by the task; and two systemctl reboots (cmd-a6514587cb4e4015, cmd-5505567c657244ce), required by the independent restart-evidence protocol. No unnecessary mutations, abandoned experiments, or failed services were observed. The fixed after_executor snapshot shows package-health clean and failed-services empty on both nodes. The only minor residue is a /tmp/reboot.log file left on node1 (and presumably node2) from the nohup reboot command, a trivial and expected byproduct of the reboot protocol, not something the executor was asked to clean up.
